about: Coupon codes and automatic sales: every COUPON_* error, hidden and personal codes, paused offers, item targets (product, category, brand, collection), percent caps, free_delivery, best offer (a sale that saves more beats a typed code: COUPON_BETTER_OFFER from quoteOrder only, placeOrder just charges the lower price), usage counting (a cancelled order frees its use), the coupon rate limit (10 failed lookups per 10 minutes), listing visibility (offerOpenFor = private.offer_open) and savePromotion validation. Ported from supabase/tests/offers.test.sql, supabase/tests/best_offer.test.sql and scripts/api_e2e.py offers_checks, with the semantics of evaluate_promotion / price_lines (20261030000260_best_offer.sql). Code checks run in this order: COUPON_RATE_LIMIT, COUPON_NOT_FOUND (unknown, paused, someone else's personal code), COUPON_NOT_STARTED, COUPON_EXPIRED, COUPON_USED_UP, COUPON_LIMIT_REACHED, COUPON_FIRST_ORDER, COUPON_ONLINE_ONLY, COUPON_NOT_APPLICABLE (no covered line), COUPON_MIN_ORDER (on covered lines), then COUPON_NOT_APPLICABLE again when the saving (base fee + discount − fee) is not positive. A use = a redemption whose order is not cancelled (redemptions.active, promotions.usesActive). Automatic sales p31-p37 (offers.test.sql:268) and the best-offer pair p40/p41 (v5/v6 here are best_offer.test.sql's phone and cable) appear only in the cases that use them; startsAt "@now-1h" stands for the SQL's now(). Conventions beyond vector-format.md: a doc in "given" replaces the world doc of the same path whole (every given doc is written in full). A field expected as null matches null or absent. orders items[] are listed in variant-id order; match them by id. "$orderId" / "$id" = the id the call returned. A "then" key ending in "/*" means the one doc in that collection (the case starts with none there); "<collection>/*": null means the call creates none. Where an expected value was not asserted by the SQL test but re-derived from the SQL code (price_lines, evaluate_promotion, offer_open, reward_referral, apply_referral_code), the case "about" says "derived".

cases.about: A failed lookup is recorded for the rate limit (price_lines inserts a coupon_attempts row).
₹500 of accessories < the ₹600 minimum, though the cart is ₹10,500; detail = the minimum in paise (offers.test.sql:160).
kind free_delivery: discount 0, fee 0 (saving = the 4900 fee).
Derived: evaluate_promotion counts only orders whose status is not cancelled.

Uses count only orders that are not cancelled (promotion_uses); admin_promotions then shows uses 0 (api_e2e.py "admin_promotions counts uses over orders that are not cancelled"); its discount total sums the same orders (derived).
No silent fallback to plain prices. SQL rolls the failed lookup back, so placeOrder does not count it toward the rate limit.
The refused checkout leaves the cart alone (offers.test.sql:238).
The tenth wrong guess in 10 minutes is still answered COUPON_NOT_FOUND and recorded.
Phones 5% and Ends soon both save 50000; Ends soon ends first. First order deal is out (alice has an order), Online deal is out (COD), the paused and future sales never count.
Recorded with its promotion and no code (offers.test.sql:286-287); the redemption and counters are derived from place_order.
5% of 5000000 capped at maxDiscountPaise 200000; total derived.
The quote charges the sale (offers.test.sql:31-33: discount, title, COUPON_BETTER_OFFER).
placeOrder never raises COUPON_BETTER_OFFER: it charges the lower price. Order discount 200000 with no code; the code has no redemption (best_offer.test.sql:38-41).
The sale covers only best-offer-phone; on the cable alone the code is the better offer, with no complaint (best_offer.test.sql:46). Total derived.
Signed out, the per-user and first-order rules do not apply.
A hidden offer has uid null and so does the signed-out caller: SQL p.uid = p_uid is NULL (not true) here, so uid null never matches a null caller.
Derived from offer_open: usesTotal ≥ usageLimit.
Derived from offer_open: usesByUser ≥ perUserLimit (signed in only).
Derived: offer_open has no code condition, so a running public sale is listed.
Detail = the SQL constraint name; the other value rules under it: flat ≥ 100, free_delivery = 0.
SQL detail is Postgres's "invalid input value for enum ..." text, so no errorDetail is fixed here.
Codes are compared trimmed and uppercased: "welcome" is WELCOME.
Defaults from the promotions table: perUserLimit 1 (not unlimited), isPublic, isActive, startsAt now; the code is trimmed and uppercased.
Left-out keys and targets are kept (offers.test.sql:459-460).

notExpressed.why: offers_for_product = offer_open + covers(promotion, product); the call list has no pure covers() call. covers() itself is exercised by the product/category/brand/collection quote cases.
offer_products (the /offers/:id product list, hidden/personal offers empty except for their owner) is a catalogue listing, not a callable in the contract list.

available_offers row shape (id, title, description, code, kind, value, maxDiscountPaise, minSubtotalPaise, startsAt, endsAt, appliesTo, automatic): publicOffers is a stored doc shape, no call returns it.
Covered by every quote case (promotion is always {id, title, code, kind}); no separate case.
admin_promotions status (paused, ended, scheduled, running) is derived from isActive/startsAt/endsAt on the staff screen; no call in the contract returns it.
Promotion banner sync (offers.test.sql:319-362) is not a money rule; not ported in this file.
Concurrency (the promotion lock): needs parallel callers against the emulator. The sequential effect is usage-limit-counts-the-whole-shop / place-refuses-a-used-up-code.
Razorpay create-payment / webhook amount checks on a discounted order: dropped (decision D4).
RLS/grant checks (promotions, targets, redemptions, coupon_attempts, referral tables) are ported with the rules tests.
